howDoI.q: How do I make an AND, so two things must both happen before something opens?
How do I make one monster stop another?
How do I make a monster turn into another when Lami touches it?
How do I make a block that sends out a monster every few seconds?
How do I make a monster add to a counter when Lami touches it?
How do I make a puzzle where three things must all be on?

pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Both Together is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a few minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the gate at the end of a level to go on.

A spark runs along a wire in the sky, with dials hanging on it. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Both Together
pages.html:
Level 1: Both Together

The A SPARK RUNS THE WIRE sign stands near the start. The box in the left wall sends a spark along the wire every few seconds. Two dials hang on the wire, both off, and a dark lamp sits on a post at the far end.

The JUMP TO BUMP A DIAL ON sign says what to do. Jump under a dial and it flips on, from a red lamp to a green one.

The ONE DIAL OFF STOPS THE SPARK sign says what you will see if you turn on only one. The spark runs through the dial that is on, and dies at the dial that is off.

Turn on both and a spark reaches the lamp. The lamp lights, and its light slides down the post. The THE LIGHT DROPS. TOUCH IT sign says to pick it up. The THE LIGHT OPENS THIS GATE sign stands by the gate, which is the way out. There are five coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The spark box. In gate.bbl the box is a solid block with a monster to give birth to (the spark) and a number of ticks between births. Open one.map to see it set into the left wall.
  • The spark. Open one.mon in the monsters editor and pick the spark. Its Power is 80, and its Lives is Until the end of its path, so it disappears after it reaches the lamp. Its path runs 23 blocks right and then up the post, following the wire you can see.
  • The dials. A dial that is off has Power 90, stronger than the spark. When they meet, the weaker one is destroyed, so the spark dies. A dial that is on has Power 80, the same as the spark, and monsters of the same power pass through each other. Both dials are placed on the map as the one that is off.
  • Turning a dial on. The dial that is off has a Power under 100, which means Lami destroys it by touching it. When destroyed it becomes the dial that is on. The dial that is on has Lives Forever (indestructible), so touching it again does nothing, and it stays on.
  • The lamp. The dark lamp has Power 70, weaker than the spark, and it becomes the falling light when destroyed. A spark is the only thing that can reach it: it hangs higher than Lami can jump.
  • The light. The falling light has Power 200 and its path runs 8 blocks down. At the end of its path it becomes the resting light, which is indestructible. In gate.mbl the resting light's picture adds 1 to counter 22 when Lami touches it.
  • The gate. In gate.bbl the gate takes 1 from counter 22. With none to spend, the gate stays shut. Lami starts with 1 and a counter shows one less than it holds, so they need the light to open it.
  • The signs. Each sign is a few ordinary blocks side by side, with the words drawn in their pictures.

pages.head: Level 2: All Three
pages.html:
Level 2: All Three

The ALL THREE MUST BE ON sign stands near the start. The wire has three dials now, and it does not run straight: it climbs up past a ladder, along over a grass ledge, and comes down again before it runs on to the lamp.

The THE WIRE CLIMBS. SO DOES LAMI sign stands by the ladder. One dial hangs over the ledge, so Lami has to climb up and walk into it.

The A DIAL STAYS ON sign says that a dial you have turned on stays on. Turn them on in any order, take your time, and the next spark that passes all three lights the lamp. The ALL ON? LAMP LIGHTS sign says so. There are eight coins.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • One more dial. Open two.map. Three monsters of the dial that is off are placed along the wire. Nothing else changes: the spark has to get past every one of them, and one that is off is enough to stop it.
  • A wire that bends. Open two.mon and pick the spark. Its path has seven corners: right, up, right, down, right, and up to the lamp. The wire pictures on the map only show where the path goes. A spark follows its path, not the wire.
  • The dial on the ledge. The third dial is placed at the top of the wire, over a ledge of grass and dirt blocks. It is the same monster as the others. Lami touches it by walking along the ledge, because its picture is not solid.
  • Why the order does not matter. A dial that has been turned on never turns off. So it makes no difference which dial Lami turns on first.
  • The exit. The gate links to the The End scene in gate.gam, which plays the ending.

pages.head: What it cannot do
pages.html:
What it cannot do

An AND here is monsters meeting, and that is all it is:

  • There is no OR. Any dial that is off kills the spark. For an OR you would run a second wire with its own spark to the same lamp, and the lamp needs one spark from either.
  • There is no NOT, and a dial cannot be turned off again. A monster turns into another one only when it is destroyed, and the dial that is on cannot be destroyed.
  • A spark does not stop and wait for a dial. It is born on a timer and runs its path, so a dial turned on just after a spark passed has to wait for the next one.
  • Nothing counts how many dials are on. The lamp lights only because a spark got to it.
  • A monster never touches background blocks, so the lamp has to be a monster. Only a background block can open a gate, so the lamp's light is a monster picture that adds to a counter, and the gate takes it from there.
  • A path has at most 10 corners, so a wire cannot bend more than that. The monster file holds 64 monsters.
  • The wire pictures are only pictures. The spark runs the monster's path, whatever is drawn on the map.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

Try one change at a time, and play after each:

  • Change the power of the dial that is on to 70. The spark kills it, and nothing ever passes it.
  • Change the power of the dial that is off to 80. The spark passes through, and the dial is no use.
  • In gate.bbl, change the spark box's number of ticks between births. A shorter time sends sparks more often.
  • Place a fourth dial on the map, and lengthen the spark's path to match.
  • Place a second wire with its own box, its own spark and its own path to the same lamp, and you have an OR.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.

box.tagline: Both dials on, or no light.
box.back: A small explorer in a red beanie finds a wire in the sky with dials on it. Bump each dial on, and the spark runs through to the lamp. Leave one off and the spark stops there. It is all monster power: the stronger monster wins and equal ones pass. Play, then open the game in Game-Maker and change a power.
features: Signs in the levels explain each idea
Monsters that meet compare power, which makes an AND
Made to be copied and taken apart

blurb: Two short levels about an AND. A spark runs along a wire in the sky, and two dials hang on it. Lami jumps to bump each dial on. A dial that is off stops the spark, one that is on lets it through, and only a spark that passes every dial lights the lamp. Signs in the levels say how. Play it, then open it in Game-Maker and change a monster's power.

57.long: Jump. Steer with Left and Right while you are in the air.
